en: Dhātukathā 2 Niddesa 2.14.
Exposition of the Fourteenfold Method: The Exposition of the Terms Concerning What is Included and Not Included by Way of Dissociation.
2.14.1. Aggregates, etc.

Those phenomena that are dissociated from the aggregate of material form (rūpakkhandha)—by how many aggregates, by how many bases (āyatana), and by how many elements (dhātu) are those phenomena comprised?
Those phenomena are comprised by four aggregates, two bases, and eight elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by one aggregate, ten bases, and ten elements.
Those phenomena which [are not included] by the feeling aggregate...

Those phenomena that are included in the aggregate of perception … those phenomena that are included in the aggregate of volitional formations … those phenomena that are included in the aggregate of consciousness …

Those phenomena that are dissociated from the mind-base (*manāyatana*) … those phenomena that are dissociated from the mind-faculty (*manindriya*): by how many aggregates (*khandha*), how many bases (*āyatana*), and how many elements (*dhātu*) are they comprised?
Excluding the unconditioned (*asaṅkhata*) from the category of aggregates, those phenomena are comprised by one aggregate, eleven bases, and eleven elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by four aggregates, one base, and seven elements.
Those phenomena which are the eye-base... [and so on].

Those phenomena that are dissociated from the sense-base of the tangible … those phenomena that are dissociated from the eye-element … [and so on] … those phenomena that are dissociated from the tangible-element … [and so on].
Those phenomena are included within four aggregates, two bases, and eight elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included within one aggregate, ten bases, and ten elements.
Those phenomena belonging to the eye-consciousness element...
those phenomena belonging to the ear-consciousness element...
those phenomena belonging to the nose-consciousness element...
Those phenomena belonging to the tongue-consciousness element … those phenomena belonging to the body-consciousness element … those phenomena belonging to the mind-element …
Those phenomena that are dissociated from the mind-consciousness element—
excluding the unconditioned from among the aggregates— are included within five aggregates, twelve bases, and seventeen elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included by any aggregates (khandha), nor by any bases (āyatana), but are included by one element (dhātu).
2.14.2. Truths, etc.:
Those phenomena that are dissociated from the truth of suffering (dukkhasacca) ...
Those phenomena are included within four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included within one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
Those phenomena which are dissociated from the truth of the origin and those phenomena which are dissociated from the truth of the path—
excluding the unconditioned from the classification of aggregates— are included within five aggregates, twelve bases, and eighteen elements.
By how many [factors] are they not included?
They are not included by any aggregates (khandha), nor by any bases (āyatana), nor by any elements (dhātu).
As for those phenomena that are [included] by the truth of cessation (nirodhasacca) …
Those phenomena [known] by means of the eye-faculty … those phenomena [known] by means of the body-faculty … those phenomena [known] by means of the female-faculty …
Those phenomena dissociated from the male faculty are included within four aggregates, two bases, and eight elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included by one aggregate, ten bases, or ten elements.
Those phenomena that are associated with the faculty of pleasure...
those phenomena that are associated with the faculty of pain...

Those states that are dissociated from the faculty of mental joy (somanassindriya) … those states that are dissociated from the faculty of mental grief (domanassindriya) … excluding the unconditioned from among the aggregates,
these states are comprised within five aggregates, twelve bases, and eighteen elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by any aggregates, not by any bases, and not by any elements.
By the equanimity faculty, those phenomena with which it is dissociated...
Excluding those phenomena from the category of the unconditioned, they are comprised within five aggregates, twelve bases, and thirteen elements.
Within how many are they not comprised?
They are not comprised within any aggregates, nor within any bases, but they are not comprised within five elements.
Those phenomena [arisen] through the faculty of faith … those phenomena through the faculty of energy … those phenomena through the faculty of mindfulness …

Those phenomena [arisen] through the faculty of concentration … those phenomena [arisen] through the faculty of wisdom … those phenomena [arisen] through the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown" …
The states associated with the faculty of final knowledge;
the states associated with the faculty of one who has already known;
the states associated with ignorance.
Those phenomena that are dissociated from the volitional formations conditioned by ignorance—
excluding the unconditioned from the classification of aggregates— are included within five aggregates, twelve bases, and eighteen elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not uncomprised by any aggregates, any bases, or any elements.
Those phenomena [arisen] through the condition of volitional formations with consciousness as their cause...
those phenomena [arisen] through the condition of the six sense bases with contact as their cause...
Regarding those phenomena dissociated from feeling with contact as condition:
setting aside the unconditioned as a category, those phenomena are included in one aggregate, eleven bases, and eleven elements.
In how many are they not included?
They are not included within four aggregates, one base, and seven elements.
Those phenomena which [arise] with feeling as condition for craving...
those phenomena which [arise] with craving as condition for clinging...
Those states that are dissociated from the kamma-process existence—
excluding the unconditioned from among the aggregates— are included within five aggregates, twelve bases, and eighteen elements.
From how many are they not included?
They are not uncomprised by any aggregates, any bases, or any elements. Those phenomena that belong to the existence of rebirth...
those phenomena that belong to the existence of perception...
Those phenomena that are dissociated from five-aggregate existence are included within four aggregates, two bases, and three elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included in one aggregate, ten bases, and fifteen elements.
Those phenomena that are dissociated from the sense-sphere existence (kāmabhava) are included in four aggregates, two bases, and five elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by one aggregate (khandha), ten bases (āyatana), and thirteen elements (dhātu).
Those phenomena which belong to the form realm (rūpabhava) …
Those phenomena that are dissociated from non-percipient existence ...
those phenomena that are dissociated from one-aggregate existence ...
those phenomena that are dissociated from lamentation ...
Those phenomena are included within four aggregates, two bases, and eight elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included within one aggregate, ten bases, and ten elements.

Those phenomena that belong to the formless existence (arūpabhava) … those phenomena that belong to the existence of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (nevasaññānāsaññābhava) … those phenomena that belong to the fourfold existence (catuvokārabhava) …
Those phenomena [associated] with sorrow … those phenomena [associated] with suffering … those phenomena [associated] with mental distress …

Those phenomena that [are abandoned] by means of distress… those phenomena that [are developed] by means of the foundations of mindfulness… those phenomena that [are developed] by means of the right efforts…
Those phenomena that [arise] through the basis of psychic power...
those phenomena that [arise] through meditative absorption...
those phenomena that [arise] through the immeasurables...
Those phenomena which [are associated] with the five faculties...
those phenomena which [are associated] with the five powers...
those phenomena which [are associated] with the seven factors of enlightenment...
Those phenomena dissociated from the noble eightfold path—
excluding the unconditioned from the classification of aggregates— are included within five aggregates, twelve bases, and eighteen elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not uncomprised by any aggregates, nor by any bases, nor by any elements.
2.14.3. The Heptad of Contact and so forth:
Those phenomena which [are associated] with contact...
Those phenomena that belong to feeling… those phenomena that belong to perception… those phenomena that belong to volition…
Those phenomena that are dissociated from consciousness and those phenomena that are dissociated from attention—
excluding the unconditioned from the classification of aggregates— are included within one aggregate, eleven bases, and eleven elements.
By how many [factors] are they not included?
They are not included by four aggregates (khandha), one base (āyatana), and seven elements (dhātu).
Those phenomena that are dissociated from resolve (adhimokkha) …
Excluding those states from the category of the unconditioned, they are included within five aggregates, twelve bases, and seventeen elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included in any aggregates, not included in any bases, and not included in one element.
2.14.4. Triads:
Those states that [arise] with wholesome states;
those states that [arise] with unwholesome states.
Those phenomena associated with pleasant feeling;
those phenomena dissociated from painful feeling—
excluding the unconditioned from the perspective of the aggregates— these phenomena are included within the five aggregates, the twelve bases, and the eighteen elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by any aggregates, not by any bases, and not by any elements.
Those phenomena which are dissociated from indeterminate phenomena...
Those phenomena are included within four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included within one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
Those phenomena which are dissociated from the states associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling,
and those phenomena which are dissociated from resultant states—
excluding the unconditioned from the category of aggregates— these phenomena are comprised within five aggregates, twelve bases, and thirteen elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by any aggregates, not by any bases, and not by five elements.
Those states which are states with the nature of being resultant...
Those states which are dissociated from defiled and defilement-associated states—
excluding the unconditioned from the classification of aggregates— are included within five aggregates, twelve bases, and eighteen elements.
From how many are they not included?
There are no phenomena that are not included by any aggregates, any bases, or any elements. There are those phenomena which are neither resultant nor subject to resultancy;
there are those phenomena which are neither clung-to nor subject to clinging.
Those phenomena which are dissociated from phenomena that are neither clung-to nor subject to clinging,
and those which are dissociated from phenomena that are neither defiled nor subject to defilement,
are comprised within four aggregates, two bases, and eight elements.
By how many [factors] are they not included?
They are not included by one aggregate (khandha), ten bases (āyatana), and ten elements (dhātu).
Those phenomena which are dissociated from phenomena that are both acquired and subject to clinging...
Those phenomena are included within four aggregates, two bases, and three elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included within one aggregate, ten bases, and fifteen elements.
Those states which are dissociated from states that are undefiled but subject to defilement are included within four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included in one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
Those phenomena dissociated from states with applied thought and sustained thought—
excluding the unconditioned from the perspective of aggregates— are included in five aggregates, twelve bases, and seventeen elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by any aggregates, not by any bases, but are included by one element.
Those phenomena which are associated with states that are without initial application and have only sustained application...
Those states which are dissociated from states accompanied by rapture,
and those states which are dissociated from states accompanied by pleasure—
excluding the unconditioned from the classification of aggregates— these states are included within the five aggregates, the twelve bases, and the eighteen elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by any aggregates (khandha), by any bases (āyatana), or by any elements (dhātu).
Those phenomena which are dissociated from phenomena that are without initial application and sustained application (avitakka-avicāra) …
Those phenomena are included within four aggregates, two bases, and three elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by one aggregate, ten bases, and fifteen elements.
Those states that are dissociated from states associated with equanimity—
excluding the unconditioned from the classification of aggregates— are included within five aggregates, twelve bases, and thirteen elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included by any aggregates, nor by any bases, but they are included by five elements.
Those phenomena which are to be abandoned by vision...
those phenomena which are to be abandoned by cultivation...
Those phenomena which [are associated] with phenomena whose roots are to be abandoned by vision;
those phenomena which [are associated] with phenomena whose roots are to be abandoned by cultivation;
those phenomena which [are associated] with phenomena leading to accumulation...
Those phenomena which [are related] to the phenomena leading to diminution;
those phenomena which [are related] to the phenomena of the trainee (sekha);
those phenomena which [are related] to the phenomena of the adept (asekha).
Those states that are dissociated from sublime states—
excluding the unconditioned from the classification of aggregates— are included in five aggregates, twelve bases, and eighteen elements.
In how many are they not included?
They are not uncomprised by any aggregates, any bases, or any elements.
Those phenomena which are neither to be abandoned by vision nor by cultivation...
those phenomena which have as their causes neither what is to be abandoned by vision nor what is to be abandoned by cultivation...
Those phenomena which are dissociated from phenomena that neither lead to accumulation nor lead to diminution;
those phenomena which are dissociated from phenomena that are neither-learner-nor-non-learner;
and those phenomena which are dissociated from limited phenomena.
Those phenomena are included within four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included within one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
Those phenomena which are dissociated from immeasurable phenomena ... from sublime phenomena ...
are comprised within four aggregates, two bases, and eight elements.
By how many [factors] are they not included?
They are not included by one aggregate (khandha), ten bases (āyatana), and ten elements (dhātu).
Those phenomena which are dissociated from phenomena that have limited objects...
Excluding those phenomena from the category of the unconditioned, they are comprised within five aggregates, twelve bases, and twelve elements.
Within how many are they not comprised?
They are not comprised within any aggregates, nor within any bases; they are not comprised within six elements.
Those states which [arise] through states having exalted objects;
those states which [arise] through states having immeasurable objects;
those states which [arise] through inferior states.
Those phenomena [conditioned] by phenomena fixed in falsehood;
those phenomena [conditioned] by phenomena fixed in rightness;
those phenomena [conditioned] by phenomena having the Path as their object.
Those states which are dissociated from states having the Path as their cause,
and those states which are dissociated from states having the Path as their dominant influence—
excluding the unconditioned from among the aggregates— these states are comprised within the five aggregates, the twelve bases, and the eighteen elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by any aggregates, not by any bases, and not by any elements.
Those states which are among the middle states...
Those states that are dissociated from the indeterminate states are included within four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included by one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
Those phenomena which [are related] to phenomena that have arisen...
those phenomena which [are related] to phenomena that have not yet arisen...
Those phenomena which [arise] with phenomena that have arisen...
those phenomena which [arise] with past phenomena...
those phenomena which [arise] with future phenomena...
Those phenomena which [are related] to present phenomena;
those phenomena which [are related] to internal phenomena;
those phenomena which [are related] to external phenomena.
Those phenomena which are dissociated from phenomena that are visible and impinging,
and those phenomena which are dissociated from phenomena that are invisible but impinging,
are comprised within four aggregates, two bases, and eight elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by one aggregate (khandha), ten bases (āyatana), and ten elements (dhātu).
Those phenomena which [are associated] with phenomena having past objects...
Those states which are dissociated from states having future objects;
those states which are dissociated from states having internal objects;
those states which are dissociated from states having external objects.
Excluding the unconditioned from the category of aggregates, those phenomena are included within five aggregates, twelve bases, and eighteen elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not excluded by any aggregates, nor by any bases, nor by any elements; they are not excluded by any at all.
Those states which are dissociated from states having present objects,
and those states which are dissociated from states having internal and external objects—
excluding the unconditioned from the perspective of the aggregates— these states are included within the five aggregates, the twelve bases, and the twelve elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by any aggregates (khandha), nor by any bases (āyatana), but they are not included by six elements (dhātu).
2.14.5.1. Group on Causes (Hetugocchaka) Those phenomena which [arise] with phenomena that are causes...
those phenomena which [arise] with phenomena that possess a cause...
Those phenomena which [arise] with phenomena associated with roots;
those phenomena which [arise] with both roots and root-possessing phenomena;
those phenomena which [arise] with phenomena that are root-possessing but are not themselves roots.
Those phenomena that are dissociated from both root-causes and phenomena associated with root-causes;
those phenomena that are dissociated from phenomena associated with root-causes but are not themselves root-causes;
and those phenomena that are dissociated from phenomena that are neither root-causes nor accompanied by root-causes.
Setting those phenomena aside from the category of the unconditioned, they are included within the five aggregates, the twelve bases, and the eighteen elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not excluded by any aggregates, nor by any bases, nor by any elements.
Those phenomena that are dissociated from rootless phenomena;
those phenomena that are dissociated from phenomena dissociated from roots;
those phenomena that are dissociated from phenomena that are neither root nor rootless.
Those phenomena are included within four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included within one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
2.14.5.2. The Minor Intermediate Dyads (Cūḷantaraduka):
Those phenomena [associated] with phenomena that are without conditions;
those phenomena [associated] with phenomena that are unconditioned.
Those phenomena which [are associated] with phenomena that are visible;
those phenomena which [are associated] with phenomena that are impinging;
those phenomena which [are associated] with phenomena that are material.
Those states that are dissociated from supramundane states are included within four aggregates, two bases, and eight elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included in one aggregate, ten bases, and ten elements.
Those phenomena that are dissociated from worldly phenomena are included in four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
By how many [factors] are they not included?
They are not included by one aggregate (khandha), ten bases (āyatana), and sixteen elements (dhātu).
2.14.5.3. The Group on the Taints (āsava-gocchaka).
Those phenomena which [are associated] with the taints;
those phenomena which [are associated] with phenomena associated with the taints;
those phenomena which [are associated] with both the taints and with phenomena possessing taints.
Those phenomena which are associated with the taints (āsava) and the phenomena associated with the taints;
those phenomena which are dissociated from the phenomena associated with the taints but are not themselves taints—

excluding the unconditioned (asaṅkhata) from the perspective of the aggregates (khandha)— these phenomena are comprised within the five aggregates, the twelve bases (āyatana), and the eighteen elements (dhātu).
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by any aggregates (khandha), nor by any bases (āyatana), nor by any elements (dhātu).
As for those phenomena that are with taints (sāsava), those phenomena which...
Those phenomena which are dissociated from phenomena that are dissociated from the taints (āsava);
those phenomena which are associated with the taints but are not themselves taints;
and those phenomena which are dissociated from phenomena that are both dissociated from the taints and associated with the taints.
Those phenomena are included within four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included within one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements.

Those phenomena which are dissociated from the phenomena that are untainted (anāsava), and those phenomena which are dissociated from the phenomena that are dissociated from the taints (āsavavippayutta) and untainted—
those phenomena are comprised within four aggregates (khandha), two bases (āyatana), and eight elements (dhātu).
By how many [categories] are they not included?
They are not included by one aggregate (khandha), ten bases (āyatana), and ten elements (dhātu).
2.14.5.4–9. The Group on Fetters (saṃyojana-gocchaka), etc.
Those phenomena that [are associated] with the fetters;
those phenomena that [are associated] with the ties;
those phenomena that [are associated] with the floods...
Those phenomena which [are opposed] to the factors of enlightenment;
those phenomena which [are opposed] to the hindrances;
those phenomena which [are opposed] to the perversions.
Those phenomena associated with the perversions,
and those phenomena dissociated from both the perversions and the objects pervaded by them—
excluding the unconditioned from the classification of aggregates— these phenomena are comprised within the five aggregates, the twelve bases, and the eighteen elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by any aggregates, nor by any bases, nor by any elements.
Those phenomena which [are not included] among the phenomena that are clung to...
Those phenomena which are dissociated from states associated with the taints (*parāmāsa*);
those phenomena which are both objects of the taints and not themselves taints;
and those phenomena which are dissociated from states that are both dissociated from the taints and objects of the taints.
Those phenomena are included within four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included within one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
Those phenomena which are dissociated from those phenomena that are not adhered to by clinging—
those phenomena are comprised within four aggregates, two bases, and eight elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by one aggregate (khandha), ten bases (āyatana), and ten elements (dhātu).
2.14.5.10. The Great Intermediate Dyad (Mahantaraduka).
Those phenomena which [are associated] with phenomena possessing objects;
those phenomena which [are associated] with mind;
those phenomena which [are associated] with mental factors.
Those phenomena which [arise] with phenomena associated with consciousness;
those phenomena which [arise] with phenomena conjoined with consciousness;
those phenomena which [arise] with phenomena conjoined with and originated by consciousness.

Those phenomena which are dissociated from those phenomena that are conjoined with, originated by, and co-existent with consciousness; and those phenomena which are dissociated from those phenomena that follow after consciousness—
excluding the unconditioned from the classification of aggregates— these are comprised within one aggregate, eleven bases, and eleven elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by four aggregates, one base, and seven elements.
Those phenomena which [are not included] by phenomena that lack an object...
Those phenomena which [arise] with phenomena dissociated from consciousness...
those phenomena which [arise] with phenomena associated with consciousness...
those phenomena which [arise] with derived phenomena...

Those phenomena which are dissociated from phenomena not acquired by clinging (*anupādinnā dhammā*) are included within four aggregates (*khandha*), two bases (*āyatana*), and eight elements (*dhātu*).
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included in one aggregate, ten bases, and ten elements.
Those phenomena which are dissociated from phenomena that are clung-to are included in four aggregates, two bases, and three elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by one aggregate (khandha), ten bases (āyatana), and fifteen elements (dhātu).
2.14.5.11. The Group on Grasping (Upādāna-gocchaka).
Those phenomena which [arise] from phenomena that are objects of clinging...
those phenomena which [arise] from phenomena that are defilements...
those phenomena which [arise] from phenomena that are defiled...
Those phenomena which [arise] together with defiled states;
those phenomena which [arise] together with both defilements and defiling states;
those phenomena which [arise] together with both defilements and defiled states.
Those phenomena which are dissociated from both defiled phenomena that are not themselves defilements...
those phenomena which are dissociated from both defilements and phenomena associated with defilements...
those phenomena which are dissociated from both phenomena associated with defilements and phenomena that are not themselves defilements...
Setting aside the unconditioned from the perspective of the aggregates, those phenomena are included within five aggregates, twelve bases, and eighteen elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not unincluded by any aggregates, nor by any bases, nor by any elements.
2.14.5.12. The Group on Defilements (Kilesagocchaka):
Those phenomena [associated] with defiled phenomena...
those phenomena [associated] with undefiled phenomena...
Those phenomena that are dissociated from phenomena associated with the defilements;
those phenomena that are associated with the defiled but are not themselves defilements;
and those phenomena that are dissociated from phenomena that are both dissociated from the defilements and defiled.
Those phenomena are comprised within four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
Within how many are they not comprised?
They are not comprised within one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
Those phenomena which are dissociated from phenomena that are non-defiled,
and those phenomena which are dissociated from phenomena that are both dissociated from defilements and non-defiled—
these phenomena are comprised within four aggregates, two bases, and eight elements.
By how many [categories] are they not included?
They are not included by one aggregate (khandha), ten bases (āyatana), and ten elements (dhātu).
2.14.5.13. Piṭṭhiduka (The Supplementary Pair).
Those phenomena which [are associated] with phenomena to be abandoned by vision;
those phenomena which [are associated] with phenomena to be abandoned by cultivation;
those phenomena which [are associated] with phenomena rooted in what is to be abandoned by vision...
Those states which are dissociated from those states whose causes are to be abandoned by cultivation—
excluding the unconditioned from the classification of aggregates— are included within five aggregates, twelve bases, and eighteen elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not uncomprised by any aggregates, by any bases, or by any elements.
Those phenomena which are not [to be abandoned] by vision...
those phenomena which are not [to be abandoned] by cultivation...
Those phenomena which are dissociated from those phenomena whose roots are to be abandoned by vision,
and those phenomena which are dissociated from those phenomena whose roots are to be abandoned by cultivation—
those phenomena are comprised within four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by one aggregate (khandha), ten bases (āyatana), and sixteen elements (dhātu).
Those phenomena which, among phenomena accompanied by applied thought (savitakka) ...

Those states that are dissociated from states accompanied by sustained application (savicāra) … excluding the unconditioned (asaṅkhata) from the classification of aggregates, those states are included in five aggregates, twelve bases, and seventeen elements.
In how many are they not included?
They are not uncomprised by any aggregates, nor by any bases, but are comprised by one element.
Those phenomena which [are comprised] by phenomena accompanied by rapture; those phenomena which [are comprised] by phenomena associated with rapture.
Those states that are dissociated from states associated with pleasure—
excluding the unconditioned from the classification of aggregates— are included in five aggregates, twelve bases, and eighteen elements.
In how many are they not included?
They are not uncomprised by any aggregates, any bases, or any elements.
Those phenomena dissociated from phenomena accompanied by equanimity—
excluding the unconditioned from the category of aggregates— are comprised by five aggregates, twelve bases, and thirteen elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by any aggregates, not by any bases, and not by five elements.
Those phenomena which [are] with respect to the phenomena of the sense-sphere...
Those phenomena which are dissociated from included phenomena … from surpassable phenomena … those phenomena are comprised within four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by one aggregate (khandha), ten bases (āyatana), and sixteen elements (dhātu).
[They are] not those phenomena belonging to the sense-sphere (kāmāvacara) which are...
Those phenomena which are dissociated from phenomena that are non-included,
and those phenomena which are dissociated from phenomena that are unsurpassed,
are comprised within four aggregates, two bases, and eight elements.
By how many are they not included?
They are not included by one aggregate (khandha), ten bases (āyatana), and ten elements (dhātu).
Those phenomena which [are not included] with the phenomena of the fine-material sphere (rūpāvacara) …
Those phenomena which [are associated] with formless-sphere phenomena...
those phenomena which [are associated] with phenomena leading to liberation...
those phenomena which [are associated] with fixed phenomena...
Those states which are dissociated from the states that are objects of the refuges—
excluding the unconditioned from the classification of aggregates— are included within five aggregates, twelve bases, and eighteen elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not uncomprised by any aggregates, by any bases, or by any elements.
They are not comprised by states belonging to the fine-material sphere;
they are not comprised by states belonging to the immaterial sphere.
Those phenomena which are dissociated from phenomena that are non-leading-out,
those phenomena which are dissociated from phenomena that are undetermined,
and those phenomena which are dissociated from phenomena that are without conflict— by how many aggregates, by how many bases, and by how many elements are those phenomena comprised?
Those phenomena are included within four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
Within how many are they not included?
They are not included within one aggregate, ten bases, and sixteen elements.
The sense-base of mental phenomena is the element of mental phenomena;
then there is vitality, name-and-form,
the sixfold sense-base, and birth, aging, and death.
And two triads are not obtained.
There are seven in the first interval,
ten in the cluster, and ten at the end.
Fourteen and six at the summit—
these forty-seven states are not found in the stage of complete eradication.
"And by way of a foolish question.
[47] The fourteenth exposition of the terms "included" and "not included" by way of dissociation is finished.
The *Dhātukathāpakaraṇa* (The Book of Analysis of Elements) is completed.
